summary: Treat readable.push(null) as the EOF signal, not as an ordinary null chunk.

target.notes: Queue EOF after already-buffered data; no further normal chunks may be pushed, and 'end' is emitted only after all data has been consumed.

caveats: In objectMode, null is still reserved for EOF and cannot be a data item.
An immediate C# close would be wrong if buffered chunks remain.

tests.name: buffer drains before end
tests.input: const {Readable}=require('node:stream'); const r=new Readable({read(){}}); const out=[]; r.on('data',x=>out.push(x.toString())); r.on('end',()=>console.log(out.join(','))); r.push('a'); r.push(null);

tests.name: null not object-mode data
tests.input: const {Readable}=require('node:stream'); const r=new Readable({objectMode:true,read(){this.push(null)}}); let n=0; r.on('data',()=>n++); r.on('end',()=>console.log(n));
